summary: Explains collection naming (namespace.name, valid Python identifiers, usually lowercase), checking Galaxy for conflicts, the special ansible, community and local namespaces, and requesting a new Galaxy namespace through the Ansible forum.
questions: What characters are allowed in a collection name?
Which namespace should I use for collections that only live on my machine?
Can I publish a collection in the ansible or community namespace?
How do I request a new namespace on Galaxy?
What happens if my collection name clashes with one on Galaxy?

answer_card.title: Naming your collection
answer_card.answer_md:
- Format is `namespace.name`; both must be valid Python identifiers (ASCII letters, digits, underscores), usually lowercase.
- Check Galaxy first: a conflicting name can make `ansible-galaxy collection install` fetch the wrong collection.
- Special namespaces:
  - `ansible`: Red Hat-owned; includes built-in `ansible.builtin` and `ansible.legacy`.
  - `community`: owned by the community; request it on the forum.
  - `local`: never used on Galaxy, safe for local/private collections.
- To get a new Galaxy namespace, log in to the Ansible forum and submit a namespace request.
